results.title: Geometric-Aware Variational Inference: Robust and Adaptive Regularization with Directional Weight Uncertainty
results.content: Building on recent work in radial-directional posterior decompositions and spherical weight constraints, CAP provides the first complete theoretical framework connecting directional statistics to practical noise regularization in neural networks. We introduce Concentration-Adapted Perturbations (CAP), a variational inference framework that directly models weight posteriors on the unit hypersphere using von Mises-Fisher (vMF) distributions. Based on empirical validation against vMF samples (see Figure 1 Framework ‣ Geometric-Aware Variational Inference: Robust and Adaptive Regularization with Directional Weight Uncertainty") and Appendix A.3), a globally monotonic approximation that captures both high- behavior and low- saturation (where the vMF approaches uniform on the sphere) is given by:. Synthetic experiments are conducted to validate the analytical approximations for activation statistics ( and from Eq. 4.2.2 ‣ 4.2 Activation Statistics under the vMF Posterior ‣ 4 The Concentration-Adapted Perturbations (CAP) Framework ‣ Geometric-Aware Variational Inference: Robust and Adaptive Regularization with Directional Weight Uncertainty")). We also validate the unified KL divergence formulation (Eq. 1 Framework ‣ Geometric-Aware Variational Inference: Robust and Adaptive Regularization with Directional Weight Uncertainty")) by comparing it with the KL divergence calculated via Monte Carlo estimation between sampled vMF distributions and the uniform prior. As shown in Figure 1 Framework ‣ Geometric-Aware Variational Inference: Robust and Adaptive Regularization with Directional Weight Uncertainty")D, our analytical form closely matches the empirical KL values across the entire range of values, correctly capturing both asymptotic behaviors while providing a smooth transition between them. The implementation learns a noise scale parameter for each layer and applies the unified KL regularizer from Equation 1 Framework ‣ Geometric-Aware Variational Inference: Robust and Adaptive Regularization with Directional Weight Uncertainty") during training. The analytically derived KL divergence term (Eq. 1 Framework ‣ Geometric-Aware Variational Inference: Robust and Adaptive Regularization with Directional Weight Uncertainty")) provides principled regularization that directly relates to the effective noise scale, avoiding the heuristic penalties often used in variational dropout methods. For the activation statistics verification (Fig. 1 Framework ‣ Geometric-Aware Variational Inference: Robust and Adaptive Regularization with Directional Weight Uncertainty")), we implemented a Monte Carlo simulation sampling 10,000 weight vectors from vMF distributions with varying concentration parameters .

results.title: [2309.01030] Online Adaptive Mahalanobis Distance Estimation
results.content: Submitted on 2 Sep 2023 ([v1), last revised 30 Dec 2023 (this version, v2)]. # Title:Online Adaptive Mahalanobis Distance Estimation. Authors:Lianke Qin, Aravind Reddy, Zhao Song. View a PDF of the paper titled Online Adaptive Mahalanobis Distance Estimation, by Lianke Qin and 2 other authors. > Abstract:Mahalanobis metrics are widely used in machine learning in conjunction with methods like $k$-nearest neighbors, $k$-means clustering, and $k$-medians clustering. Despite their importance, there has not been any prior work on applying sketching techniques to speed up algorithms for Mahalanobis metrics. In this paper, we initiate the study of dimension reduction for Mahalanobis metrics. In particular, we provide efficient data structures for solving the Approximate Distance Estimation (ADE) problem for Mahalanobis distances. We first provide a randomized Monte Carlo data structure. Then, we show how we can adapt it to provide our main data structure which can handle sequences of \textit{adaptive} queries and also online updates to both the Mahalanobis metric matrix and the data points, making it amenable to be used in conjunction with prior algorithms for online learning of Mahalanobis metrics. **** Sat, 2 Sep 2023 22:19:24 UTC (109 KB). **[v2]** Sat, 30 Dec 2023 03:11:25 UTC (190 KB). ## Access Paper:.
